heroLead: Harrisville sits near Slippery Rock in a part of Butler County where family farms have quietly held mineral interests, sometimes leased, sometimes just sitting, for generations.
intro: Harrisville is a small Butler County borough close to Slippery Rock, in farm country that's changed little in appearance even as the mineral rights beneath it have been leased, re-leased, and inherited multiple times over. Families here often aren't sure whether an old lease their parents signed is even still active.
We buy mineral and royalty interests near Harrisville, whether producing, leased and dormant, or held as an inherited fractional share.

sections.heading: Farm country on the Marcellus flank
paragraphs: This part of Butler County sits toward the edge of the Marcellus wet-gas fairway, so development has generally been lighter than the core counties to the south, with value depending on the specific tract and any nearby activity.

sections.heading: Sorting out an old family lease
paragraphs: It's common for a Harrisville-area family to have a lease signed by a previous generation with no clear record of whether it's still active. We review held-by-production and renewal language to determine current status before discussing value.

sections.heading: How we approach an offer
paragraphs: We look at lease status, producing history if any, and nearby activity, and explain what we find plainly.
Butler County's Recorder of Deeds is where we pull records to confirm current lease status if your own paperwork is incomplete.

faqs.question: How do I know if an old family lease near Harrisville is still active?
faqs.answer: We review the lease's held-by-production and renewal terms against actual well activity to determine its current status — this is a standard part of our process before discussing a purchase.

faqs.question: Is Harrisville in a heavily drilled part of Butler County?
faqs.answer: No, this area sits toward the flank of the Marcellus fairway with generally lighter development than counties further south, though specific tracts can still see activity.

faqs.question: Can you buy my interest even if the well on it stopped producing years ago?
faqs.answer: A dormant or shut-in well doesn't automatically mean no value — it depends on lease status and nearby activity, so it's worth reviewing rather than assuming.

faqs.question: How long does it typically take to confirm whether an old Harrisville lease is still active?
faqs.answer: It varies, but once we have the lease and any production records tied to it, we can usually determine held-by-production status within a short review rather than an extended process.
